neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that the accused and the complainant were on inimical terms due to land disputes and an earlier murder case. On the fateful day, the complainant was standing with his sons on the roadside. The offenders were on a tractor and stopped to attack them. The complainant and one of his sons ran towards the village. The accused gravely assaulted the elder son of the complainant and killed him. They then ran after the other son of the complainant and inflicted injuries on him, considering him dead, and left the place. The trial court found all the accused guilty and convicted them under Sections 148, 302 r/w Section 149 and Section 307 r/w Section 149 IPC. The High Court acquitted four accused of all the offences and convicted others under different sections. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of the accused, finding the evidence of the injured witness reliable and consistent, and that the exaggeration in the evidence did not change the prosecution story.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the main witnesses, including PW-5 Bhagwan Singh, as trustworthy despite their potential interest in the case. The court emphasized that the evidence of interested witnesses is not always suspect and can be accepted if found reliable.

quotes.text: It is well settled that the evidence of interested witnesses is not always suspect. It has to be scrutinized with caution and can be accepted if it is found reliable.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused were involved in a brutal murder due to previous enmity and land disputes. The evidence of the injured witness PW-5 was found to be reliable and consistent, and the eye-witnesses corroborated the prosecution's case. The court emphasized that the evidence of interested witnesses is not always suspect and can be accepted if found reliable.

quotes.text: The evidence of PWs-3, 4 and 5 also inspires confidence. So far as the main prosecution case was concerned, all the witnesses were consistent.
The presence of PW-5 at the scene of offence cannot be disputed since he was an injured witness. His evidence strengthened the prosecution case.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution witnesses exaggerated their accounts and involved acquitted accused, suggesting that the truth and falsehood were inextricably mixed. They claimed that the accused were falsely implicated due to previous enmity and that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses was unreliable.

quotes.text: These witnesses exaggerated the prosecution story and involved the acquitted accused. It is possible that even so far as the appellants are concerned, they have not come out with the truth.
The doctrine of 'falsus in uno falsus in omnibus', is clearly attracted to this case.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that the maxim 'falsus in uno falsus in omnibus' does not have the status of a rule of law in India and is merely a rule of caution. The court emphasized that courts should separate the grain from the chaff and not discard the entire evidence merely because some parts are found to be deficient.

quotes.text: It is trite that the maxim 'falsus in uno falsus in omnibus' has no application in India. It is merely a rule of caution.

Even if a major portion of evidence is found to be deficient, in case residue is sufficient to prove guilt of an accused, notwithstanding acquittal of a number of other co-accused persons his conviction can be maintained.

other_sentence_order.value: Appellant-Sheesh Ram was sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default, to further suffer six months rigorous imprisonment and to suffer rigorous imprisonment for five years and a fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default, to further suffer simple imprisonment for three months, respectively.
